column1: # support-upterm.tsv (harbor#1278) — the upterm a member laptop runs for remote support, the uptermd the hub's own relay runs, and the public relay that is never used.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The support binary is third-party code that gets a terminal on a colleague's account, so bin/member-install.sh takes
# exactly this version, by digest, and refuses anything else. relay/install.sh takes the uptermd rows the same way on the operator's relay.
# There is no default relay: upterm's relay reads terminal text in the clear and vouches for which key joined, so only a relay the hub runs
# itself is used, named by policy `support.relay` and `support.relay_key` (contracts/hub.md). With none, support is off.
# To move the version: take the digests from the release's checksums.txt, compare them with the digests GitHub lists for each asset, and read
# the release's changes to `upterm host` and `uptermd`: a flag renamed under bin/member-support.sh or relay/, or a new way to skip the prompt,
# changes what they must pass.
# COLUMNS  key <TAB> value
#   version            the upterm release, no leading v
#   sha256-linux-<a>   digest of upterm_linux_<a>.tar.gz from that release

#   uptermd-linux-<a>  digest of uptermd_linux_<a>.tar.gz: the relay, which relay/install.sh installs and tests/member/support/real-upterm.sh runs on loopback and sim-relay.sh under systemd behind Caddy. No laptop gets it
#   public-relay       upterm's public relay host. Never used: policy can't name it, and it sits in every member's sandbox.network.deniedDomains
